guarantees.claim: block_addr_limit is assigned KeccakRate[strength_i] cast to KeccakCountW for recognized strength values (L128, L224, L256, L384, L512); otherwise it is driven to '0.

assumptions.claim: strength_i must be one of the defined security strength enum values (L128, L224, L256, L384, L512) during normal operation.
assumptions.risk: If strength_i takes an invalid value, block_addr_limit defaults to '0, leading to wrong Keccak rate selection and potential incorrect KMAC output, compromising integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: The 'unique case' does not explicitly handle possible extra enum members of strength_i beyond the five listed security strengths; such values fall into the default branch, assigning '0 to block_addr_limit.
uncertain_points.cond: strength_i value outside {L128, L224, L256, L384, L512}
uncertain_points.risk: An unexpected strength value could force a zero rate, leading to incorrect Keccak padding and opening the possibility of MAC forgery or integrity bypass.
